function: Jointly selects UAV hovering spot, NOMA device activation and transmit power splitting to maximize downlink sum-rate under energy limits (p. 6, p. 7).
system: NOMA downlink from one UAV-MBS at 60 GHz, 100 MHz to 5 devices; scalar channel gains, antenna count not stated; no RIS (p. 4, p. 8, p. 9).
method: Double deep Q-network (5 fully connected layers, offline training) and cost-subsidized multiarmed bandit (UCB or MOSS, online, no DNN); reinforcement learning (p. 6, p. 9).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rician fading (parameter 10 dB) with close-in path loss (exponent 2.1, shadowing 4.4 dB); no 3GPP or measured data (p. 5, p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained offline for 100 episodes of up to 100 steps; tested over 100,000 interactions with sweeps of power, bandwidth and Rician parameter (p. 9, p. 10, p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned only: exhaustive search (upper bound), random (lower bound), conventional CSSP pairing with optimal UAV position; DDQN and CS-MAB are compared only with each other (p. 10).
metrics: Normalized ergodic sum-rate (bps/Hz), total rate (Gbps), energy per sum-rate (EU per bps/Hz), training episode reward (p. 10, p. 11, p. 12).
complexity: Deployment complexity O(vAK) for DDQN with A layers, O(vK) for CS-MAB, versus O(v*C(K,D)) for exhaustive search; K devices, v hovering spots (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 5: "given by a Rician channel representation to model the presence of the LOS signal". Path loss comes from the close-in model of [52], [53] (p. 9); custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "swept by adjusting the Rician parameter". The paper only sweeps power (Fig. 3), bandwidth (Figs. 9-10) and the Rician parameter (Fig. 11); it never states that a trained agent was tested on a scenario, band or channel not used in training.
q3_support: p. 10: "Upper and lower performance benchmark references are respectively represented by the exhaustive and random solution strategies". CSSP is also non-learned; no earlier learned method or standard learner other than the paper's own DDQN and CS-MAB is compared.
q4_support: p. 8: "The proposed DDQN agent (with A layers) has a deployment complexity of O(vAK ) for K candidate devices within an area of v hovering positions."
q5_support: p. 8: "We assume a data-offloading NOMA-UAV-MBS downlink system where 5 candidate receiving devices are scattered arbitrarily". The environment is self-simulated; no code or data link, and no public dataset, appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 6: aerial link (UAV-MBS); the agents learn NOMA power splitting and device activation jointly with the hovering spot (action vector, p. 6), so the above-PHY check is passed. Antenna configuration is not stated (scalar gains, Eq. 1, p. 4); single-antenna links are admitted for NTN. Path loss follows the close-in model of [52], [53] (p. 9), not a 3GPP model. DDQN and CS-MAB are both proposed, so neither is an earlier learned baseline (q3 = 0). q2 borderline: Fig. 11 (p. 12) sweeps the Rician parameter from -40 to 40 dB without saying whether the agent is retrained for each value, so it is not counted as a test in new conditions.
